name: Windows 10
description: Windows 10 was the long-running mainstream OS from Microsoft before Windows 11, known for broad hardware compatibility and modest requirements. It reached end of support on 14 October 2025, meaning it no longer receives security updates, though it still runs on a very wide range of older hardware.
min_cpu_intel: Any 1 GHz+ Intel processor (64-bit for 64-bit editions)
min_cpu_amd: Any 1 GHz+ AMD processor (64-bit for 64-bit editions)
requirements_notes: Minimum RAM is 1GB for 32-bit or 2GB for 64-bit. Requires DirectX 9 graphics with a WDDM 1.0 driver. Windows 10 reached end of support on 14 October 2025 (no further security updates); the final feature version is 22H2. Recommended: 4GB RAM and an SSD for comfortable performance.

name: Arch Linux
description: Arch Linux is a lightweight, rolling-release distribution built around simplicity and user control. Rather than a fixed version, it updates continuously, and the system is assembled by the user from the command line during installation. It is aimed at experienced Linux users, and its very low base requirements make it attractive for building a lean system on older hardware.
requirements_notes: Minimum RAM is about 512 MiB (more is needed to boot the live installer); a base install fits in roughly 2 GiB. Rolling release with no fixed version. 32-bit (i686) support ended in 2017. An internet connection is required during installation. A graphical desktop must be installed manually and will want 2GB+ RAM.

name: Bazzite
description: Bazzite is a gaming-focused Linux distribution built on Fedora atomic technology, designed to work out of the box on desktops, laptops, and handheld gaming PCs like the Steam Deck. It ships with gaming tools, drivers, and Steam preconfigured, and uses an image-based atomic update system for reliability.
requirements_notes: Requires an SSD for the root partition (needed by the atomic update system) and a GPU supporting Vulkan 1.3 or higher. Disks must be GPT formatted. Gaming installs need about 50GB free (120GB recommended). Rolling, image-based release rather than a fixed version.

name: CachyOS
description: CachyOS is a performance-oriented Linux distribution based on Arch, tuned with optimized compiler flags and a custom kernel for speed. It targets modern hardware and is popular with gamers and enthusiasts who want Arch power with an easier, GUI-driven installation.
min_cpu_intel: Modern 64-bit Intel CPU with x86-64-v3 support (roughly Haswell / 4th-gen or newer)
min_cpu_amd: Modern 64-bit AMD CPU with x86-64-v3 support (roughly Excavator / Zen or newer)
requirements_notes: Requires a CPU supporting the x86-64-v3 instruction set (roughly 2013-era Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or newer) — older 64-bit CPUs are NOT supported. GUI installer minimum RAM is 4GB (about 3GB absolute); 8GB recommended for KDE, Steam, and multitasking. Official minimum storage figure not published — verify.

name: Windows 11
description: Windows 11 is the latest major release of Microsoft Windows, featuring a redesigned Start menu and taskbar, tighter security defaults, and stricter hardware requirements than previous versions. Its mandatory TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot requirements make CPU generation the key factor in whether an older laptop can run it.
min_cpu_intel: 8th-gen Intel Core or newer (1 GHz+, 2+ cores, 64-bit)
min_cpu_amd: AMD Ryzen 2000 series or newer (Zen+, 1 GHz+, 2+ cores, 64-bit)
requirements_notes: CPU must be on the Microsoft approved processor list — this is the main blocker for older machines. Requires UEFI firmware with Secure Boot, DirectX 12 / WDDM 2.0 graphics, a 720p+ display 9 inches or larger, and an internet connection for initial setup (Home edition).

name: Fedora
description: Fedora Workstation is a community-driven distribution sponsored by Red Hat that ships recent versions of the Linux kernel and desktop software, making it popular with developers and enthusiasts who want up-to-date technology. It uses the GNOME desktop by default and follows a roughly six-month release cycle.
requirements_notes: Recommended: 4GB RAM (8GB+ for optimal use) and a 40GB SSD. Figures are for the Workstation (GNOME) edition. Fedora 44 ships GNOME 50 and is Wayland-only (no X.org session). Fedora follows a roughly six-month release cycle.

name: Ubuntu
description: Ubuntu is one of the most widely used Linux distributions, developed by Canonical and known for its polish, large community, and strong hardware support. The LTS (Long Term Support) releases are supported for five years, making Ubuntu a common choice for newcomers and a popular way to give older laptops a modern, secure operating system.
requirements_notes: Recommended: 4GB RAM for a comfortable GNOME desktop experience. Requires a 1024x768+ display and a GPU with at least 256MB VRAM for 3D acceleration. Ubuntu 26.04 LTS "Resolute Raccoon" ships GNOME 50 and the Linux 7.0 kernel, and is supported until April 2031. A minimal install can fit in about 8.6GB.

name: Pop!_OS
description: Pop!_OS is a Linux distribution developed by computer maker System76, based on Ubuntu and focused on a clean, productive workflow. Version 24.04 LTS introduces System76's own Rust-based COSMIC desktop environment. It offers strong out-of-the-box support for NVIDIA graphics and a polished experience aimed at developers, creators, and gamers.
requirements_notes: Secure Boot must be DISABLED in the BIOS to install. Recommended: 4GB RAM. Version 24.04 LTS uses the new Rust-based COSMIC desktop and is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Separate download images are provided for Intel/AMD graphics and for NVIDIA.

name: Linux Mint
description: Linux Mint is a popular, beginner-friendly Linux distribution based on Ubuntu, known for its familiar desktop layout, out-of-the-box multimedia support, and modest hardware demands. The flagship Cinnamon edition offers a traditional Windows-like desktop, which makes it one of the most common first steps for people moving away from Windows.
requirements_notes: Recommended for comfortable use: 4GB RAM and 100GB disk space. Display 1024x768 or higher. A dual-core CPU (e.g. Intel Core i3 / AMD Ryzen 3) is recommended for a smoother experience. Linux Mint 22.x is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and supported until 2029. Figures are for the main Cinnamon edition.

name: ChromeOS Flex
description: ChromeOS Flex is a free, cloud-first operating system from Google that installs on standard PCs and Macs — a version of ChromeOS designed to breathe new life into older hardware. It boots quickly, is managed largely through the Chrome browser and web apps, and is popular for reviving aging laptops for lightweight, secure everyday use.
requirements_notes: Installs on standard PCs and Macs and requires the ability to boot from a USB drive. Devices and integrated graphics made before around 2010 may perform poorly or be unsupported. TPM and Secure Boot are not required. Continuously updated by Google.

name: ChromeOS
description: ChromeOS is Google's cloud-first operating system that ships preinstalled on Chromebooks. Built around the Chrome browser, web apps, Android apps, and (on many models) Linux apps, it emphasizes speed, simplicity, security, and automatic updates. It is tied to Chromebook hardware and is not offered as a standalone installer for other laptops.
requirements_notes: ChromeOS comes preinstalled on Chromebooks and is not separately installable on standard laptops — for those, see ChromeOS Flex. Each Chromebook receives automatic updates until its Auto Update Expiration (AUE) date. Hardware requirements are set by the specific Chromebook model.

name: SteamOS
description: SteamOS is Valve's gaming-focused Linux distribution, built on Arch Linux and best known for powering the Steam Deck handheld. It boots into a console-like Steam Big Picture interface and uses Proton to run Windows games. As of SteamOS 3.8 it can be installed on some standard PCs, though it requires an AMD GPU and remains in beta for non-Valve hardware.
min_cpu_intel: Any 64-bit x86 Intel processor (note: Intel GPUs are only experimentally supported)
requirements_notes: Requires an AMD GPU — NVIDIA GPUs are NOT supported, and Intel GPU support is experimental and buggy. An internal NVMe SSD is required (40GB minimum; 200GB+ recommended for games). Laptop dual-GPU setups (e.g. NVIDIA Optimus) are not supported. Installing on non-Steam-Deck PCs is officially in beta. SteamOS is Arch-based and continuously updated; AMD RDNA2 (RX 6000-series) and newer work best.

name: Nobara
description: Nobara is a Fedora-based Linux distribution optimized for gaming, streaming, and content creation, maintained by Thomas "GloriousEggroll" Crider. It takes a standard Fedora desktop and adds preinstalled GPU drivers, multimedia codecs, gaming tools like Steam, Proton, Lutris, and Wine, and a custom patched kernel — removing most of the manual setup Fedora normally needs for gaming. It aims to be an approachable, out-of-the-box gaming OS for newcomers and enthusiasts alike.
requirements_notes: Recommended: a modern GPU and an SSD for gaming and content creation. NVIDIA proprietary-driver support covers Turing (RTX 20-series / GTX 16-series) and newer only — Pascal (GTX 10-series, MX250/330/350, Quadro P-series) and older are no longer supported due to NVIDIA's open-source kernel-module shift. AMD GPUs are well supported via open-source Mesa drivers. Ships with drivers, codecs, and gaming tools preinstalled; based on Fedora with a custom patched kernel and continuous updates.

name: Kubuntu
description: Kubuntu is an official flavor of Ubuntu that uses the KDE Plasma desktop instead of GNOME. It pairs Ubuntu's solid base and five-year LTS support with Plasma's highly customizable, feature-rich interface, making it a popular choice for users who want a tweakable, Windows-like desktop with the reliability of Ubuntu underneath.
requirements_notes: Recommended: 6GB RAM (8GB+ for multitasking and multi-monitor setups). Uses the KDE Plasma 6.6 desktop (Wayland by default) on a Linux 7.0 kernel. Kubuntu 26.04 LTS "Resolute Raccoon" is supported until April 2031. A GPU with basic 3D acceleration is recommended.

name: Garuda Linux
description: Garuda Linux is a performance-oriented, Arch-based rolling-release distribution known for its striking KDE Plasma (Dr460nized) desktop, gaming focus, and out-of-the-box tuning. It ships with the Zen kernel, BTRFS with automatic snapshots, a friendly graphical setup assistant, and preinstalled gaming and driver tooling — aiming to make the power of Arch approachable and visually polished.
requirements_notes: Recommended: 8GB RAM and a 50GB+ SSD (the gaming edition needs more space). A dedicated GPU with 2GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA or AMD) is recommended; OpenGL 3.3 or higher required. The 2026 ISO uses NVIDIA 590 drivers, which no longer support the GTX 1000-series (Pascal) and older. Arch-based rolling release with a Zen kernel and BTRFS snapshots.

name: Zorin OS
description: Zorin OS is an Ubuntu-based Linux distribution designed to make switching from Windows or macOS as painless as possible, with a familiar, polished desktop whose layout can mimic other operating systems. It bundles common apps, can run many Windows programs through built-in compatibility tools, and offers a lightweight Lite edition for older hardware — a popular choice for giving an aging PC a fast, modern, secure operating system.
requirements_notes: Figures are for the Core/Pro editions (GNOME). The lightweight Lite edition (XFCE) runs on far older or weaker hardware — as little as 512MB RAM and 10GB storage — making Zorin a strong option for reviving very old PCs. Zorin OS 18.1 is based on Ubuntu LTS with the Linux 6.17 kernel.

name: elementary OS
description: elementary OS is a design-focused, privacy-respecting Linux distribution based on Ubuntu LTS, known for its clean, macOS-inspired Pantheon desktop and a curated AppCenter of native apps. It emphasizes thoughtful, ethical computing with a pay-what-you-want model, making it an approachable, polished choice for people switching from macOS or Windows.
min_cpu_intel: Recent Intel Core i3 or comparable 64-bit dual-core processor
requirements_notes: An SSD is strongly recommended for good performance, and a 1024x768 or larger display and internet access are needed for installation. elementary OS 8 is based on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and defaults to a Wayland-based Secure Session; official ARM64 builds are also available.

name: Debian
description: Debian is one of the oldest and most influential Linux distributions, prized for its rock-solid stability, enormous software repository, and strict commitment to free software. It is the foundation on which Ubuntu and countless other distributions are built. With a range of desktop options and famously conservative, well-tested releases, Debian is a dependable choice for everything from reviving old hardware to running servers.
requirements_notes: Figures are for a standard desktop install (2GB recommended, 10GB+ storage). Debian is highly flexible: a lightweight desktop runs comfortably in about 1GB, and a minimal or headless install needs far less. Debian 13 "Trixie" dropped 32-bit (i386) as an installation architecture; 64-bit (amd64) and ARM are supported. It is known for its stability and as the base for Ubuntu and many other distros.
